judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same Grade rank 1) within Strand 2 ALGEBRA, but in different Sub-Strands. The second (B5.2.2.1.1, Sub-Strand 2: Algebraic Expressions) establishes the foundational conception that letters in mathematical phrases represent ordinary numbers combined with operators; the first (B5.2.3.1.1, Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations, under the Content Standard 'Solve problems involving single-variable, one-step equations') requires learners to translate a word problem into an equation in which the unknown is represented by a letter/variable. Understanding letters-as-numbers in expressions substantively supports the more complex task of modelling a problem situation as an equation with an unknown, so the second builds towards the first. This is a same-rank judgment justified by the pair-specific conceptual dependency (expression notation underpinning equation formulation), not by shared strand, code prefix, or token overlap alone; direction is asserted with moderate confidence since both sit at the same grade coordinate.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (coordinate rank 2, resolved) sharing the direct parent Content Standard B6.1.1.1 ('quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals') under Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 1: Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality. B6.1.1.1.1 models number quantities up to 1,000,000 with graph sheets and multi-base blocks; B6.1.1.1.5 rounds (off, up, down) whole numbers up to 100,000 to the nearest ten thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens. The two indicators are substantively coherent complementary skills on the same multi-digit whole-number place-value structure: concrete grouping representations and rounding to named place-value positions mutually reinforce understanding of how digits are organised by place. This coherence is pair-specific rather than generic recurrence.
